Description: Marco Sanudo, aged fifteen in 1259, is a spirited young scion of the ducal house of Naxos, younger brother to William. Fascinated by maritime navigation, rigging, and swift scout vessels, he spends every waking hour exploring the harbours and treacherous reefs of the Cyclades. Though still an esquire awaiting formal knighthood, Marco possesses remarkable sharp-eyed vigilance and archery skills, frequently assisting his elder brother in testing newly rigged patrol galleys. In 1259, amidst heightened war alerts, Marco serves as an energetic dispatch runner and coastal scout, relaying vital signal messages across the island chain. His boundless vigor and inquisitive courage make him a beloved young asset to the ducal court. Young Marco spends lively days exploring the shipwright docks and rigging lofts of Naxos harbor. Nimble and daring, he shins up topmasts in heavy swells with the agility of a veteran topman. His bright, fearless spirit lifts the spirits of all garrison troops, as he yearns eagerly to embark on his first major naval campaign and capture a hostile war banner. With boundless energy and an adventurer's spirit, Marco navigates the hidden anchorages and reefs of the Cyclades. His sharp-eyed scouting and fearless loyalty provide vital intelligence safeguarding the island fleet from surprise ambush.
Motivations: Uphold the feudal rights, defensive security, and sacred sovereignty of the Latin realms across Greece and Romania.
Ensure maximum tactical preparedness, knightly discipline, and logistical cohesion against Byzantine reconquest.
Maintain Catholic Christian communion and vital maritime communication with Western European allies and Venice.
Values: Unwavering fidelity to Catholic feudal oaths, chivalric honor, and ancestral crusader heritage.
Dedication to aristocratic solidarity, fortified defense, and protection of Christian subjects from destruction.
Pragmatic governance balancing naval commerce, legal jurisprudence, and vigilant border patrol.
Fears: Catastrophic military collapse allowing Nicaean Byzantine armies to overthrow Latin rule in Constantinople and Greece.
The loss of hereditary fiefs, fortresses, or maritime trade lifelines to enemy sieges or internal factional betrayal.
SpeechStyle: Speaks with infectious youthful enthusiasm and quick wit, bursting with eagerness to embark on grand Aegean voyages.
